expected: Persist one preference flag
contract_check: MISMATCH: keys themselves match USER_PREF_KEYS exactly, but the update semantics are broken — see code_findings.
code_findings: togglePref sends only `{ [key]: value }` (SettingsScreen.js:218), but PATCH /notifications/prefs takes the full NotificationPrefs pydantic model with `= True` defaults for every field and replaces the stored JSON wholesale (notifications/router.py:211-229, pref_dict = prefs.model_dump()).

Net effect: flipping ANY single switch off silently resets every OTHER preference (including the previously-disabled ones, and the derived book_added) back to true on the server. Turn off 'New Follower', then off 'Post Liked' — the second call resends new_follower:true by default and re-enables it. This is invisible in the UI (local `prefs` state is right) but the server-side truth drifts on every toggle after the first.
Fix needs either the backend to merge into existing stored prefs instead of replacing, or the client to send the full local `prefs` object on every toggle.
